page: Hetzner Cloud cx43 is a virtualized server instance running on the QEMU hypervisor, powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the cx43 demonstrates moderate performance across various workloads. Its stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 2548.38 and multi-core score of 20252.78 both fall within the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 888.0 GB/sec and a large block speed of 89.3 GB/sec, alongside a write speed of 62.62 GB/sec. While the instance exhibits weak performance in single-threaded gzip compression (23.39 GB/sec) and Geekbench single-core testing (1143.0), it achieves average results in multi-core Geekbench (5615.0) and software compilation (8351.0). Database operations and web serving throughput are stable, with Redis SET operations reaching 14.46 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 10.98 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and balanced hardware profile, the cx43 offers a cost-efficient solution for resource-dense workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. The combination of 8 vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and fast NVMe storage makes it suitable for general-purpose applications, development environments, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and moderate web serving. However, the shared CPU model and weaker single-core performance metrics represent a tradeoff, making it less ideal for sustained high-performance computing or large-scale LLM inference, though it can handle small-scale model inference with acceptable generation speeds.
